title: Youth justice programs: reported spending against City payments on the same agreement
question: For programs whose 2024-29 grant agreement can be told apart in the City payment table, did the City pay more than the program reported spending?
finding: 5 of 12 saved programs match exactly one youth-department agreement by title; 7 share an agreement with other programs (for example titles such as 'Productive Adult-24-29') or have none named, and are left out. None of the matched programs was paid in fiscal 2025 and 2026 more than 5% above the spending its pages report for 2024-25 and 2025-26; payments under those two year labels run at 0.84 to 0.93 times reported spending. Adding fiscal 2027 lines paid so far (which mix late 2025-26 claims with the new year's) takes every one of them above reported spending, so the two records agree within the lag of reimbursement.
how: City payments are voucher lines with department code CHF to the grantee (payee matched to its nonprofit profile), on a 2024-29 or 2026-29 agreement whose title shares a distinctive word with the program name (for example 'Young Adult Court-24-29'). Paid is summed by the year label on the line, fiscal 2025 to 2027 to date; the report's two years of expenditures are the comparison. Agreed is the supplier-contracts table's amount for that agreement number.
limits: Payments lag spending: fiscal 2027 lines include reimbursements for 2025-26 work, and a grant can be paid in advance. A grantee may hold several programs under one agreement; only single matches are shown. The comparison is a check of the department's report against the payment ledger, not an audit.
